questions.question: How many fields does the code's AB_2013_FIELDS list emit for Section 3111(a)?
options: 12 fields, including sources, purpose, size, content types, rights, processing, dates, and synthetic-data use
3 fields: owner, license, and model size
7 fields copied unchanged from a model card
30 fields including every internal training hyperparameter
questions.explanation: AB_2013_FIELDS contains twelve disclosure names. render_markdown iterates through that list, so the output is a dataset summary rather than a model card or a full internal training log.

questions.question: When does flag_followups add a CPRA-related follow-up?
options: Whenever the dataset is synthetic
When the summary marks contains_personal_information as Y
Whenever the collection date is in 2026
Only when the model has a system card
questions.explanation: The first branch checks the exact personal-information field and appends CPRA obligations when it equals Y. The toy summary uses N, so that follow-up is absent even though synthetic-data obligations may still be noted.

questions.question: What does the toy summary's uses_synthetic_data_generation = Y trigger?
options: Automatic deletion of all generated weights
A conclusion that no provenance is needed
A note that obligations may still attach to the base model used to generate the data
A waiver of all copyright and privacy checks
questions.explanation: flag_followups appends a base-model obligation for synthetic generation. Synthetic output is not a provenance blank cheque: the source model and any input data still need a governance record.

questions.question: What principle does the lesson attribute to the convergent 2025 DPA positions?
options: Public first-party content is always prohibited for training
Only synthetic text may be used after 2025
Explicit consent is always required even when safeguards exist
Legitimate interest can justify public first-party training when opt-out signals and safeguards are respected
questions.explanation: The lesson describes legitimate interest plus safeguards and opt-out handling as the common direction across the cited authorities. It is a jurisdiction-specific legal analysis, not an unconditional permission for every dataset.

questions.question: Why is collection-time governance more important than a promise to delete one record later?
options: Once information is distributed through model weights, surgical erasure is not generally available; full retraining is the expensive fallback
Models cannot contain any information after training
Regulators are forbidden from auditing deployed models
Deletion requests apply only to cookies, never to data
questions.explanation: The irreversibility problem means a training-time inclusion decision can be hard to undo. Unlearning, influence localization, and refusal fine-tuning are partial remediations, not an exact right-to-erasure operation.

questions.question: What did the Data Provenance Initiative's "Consent in Crisis" finding measure?
options: A complete replacement of web data by synthetic data
An accelerating rise in publisher robots.txt restrictions, with about 25% of top sources adding restrictions between 2023 and 2024
A stable opt-out rate with no change in publisher behaviour
A legal requirement that every publisher use the same robots.txt text
questions.explanation: The finding describes a shrinking openly trainable commons, not a new universal file format. A provenance pipeline must record and respect machine-readable restrictions before collection.
